title: Coordinate Bonding
page_title: Coordinate Bonding | Cambridge (CIE) AS Chemistry Revision Notes 2023

blocks.md:
- In **simple** **covalent** **bonds** the two atoms involved share electrons
- Some molecules have a **lone** pair of electrons that can be donated to form a bond with an **electron-deficient** atom

  - An electron-deficient atom is an atom that has an **unfilled outer orbital**
- So **both electrons** are from the **same atom**
- This type of bonding is called **dative covalent bonding** or **coordinate bond**
- An example of a dative bond is in an **ammonium ion**

  - The hydrogen ion, H<sup>+</sup> is **electron-deficient **and has space for two electrons in its shell
  - The nitrogen atom in ammonia has a lone pair of electrons which it can donate to the hydrogen ion to form a dative covalent bond

blocks.text: Coordinate bonding in the ammonium ion

blocks.alt: Dot-and-cross diagram showing an ammonia molecule donating its lone pair to a hydrogen ion, H+, to form the ammonium ion, NH4+, with the dative covalent bond drawn as an arrow from nitrogen to hydrogen.

blocks.md: ***Ammonia (NH***<sub>***3***</sub>***) can donate a lone pair to an electron-deficient proton (H***<sup>***+***</sup>***) to form a charged ammonium ion (NH***<sub>***4***</sub><sup>***+***</sup>***)***

- **Aluminium** **chloride** is also formed using dative covalent bonding
- At **high temperatures, **aluminium chloride can exist as a **monomer** (AlCl<sub>3</sub>)

  - The molecule is electron-deficient and needs two electrons to complete the aluminium atom’s outer shell
- At **lower temperatures, **the two molecules of AlCl<sub>3</sub> join together to form a more stable dimer (Al<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>6</sub>)

  - The molecules combine because lone pairs of electrons on two of the chlorine atoms form **two coordinate bonds **with the aluminium atoms

blocks.alt: Dot-and-cross diagram of two AlCl3 molecules joining to form Al2Cl6: a lone pair from a chlorine atom on each molecule forms a dative covalent bond to the aluminium atom of the other, shown by arrows from chlorine to aluminium.

blocks.md: ***Aluminium chloride is also formed with a dative covalent bond in which two of the chlorine atoms donate their lone pairs to each of the aluminium atoms to form a dimer***

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- In dative covalent bonding, both electrons in the covalent bond come from (are donated by) one atom.
- A dative covalent bond uses an arrow from the donated pair of electrons to the electron-deficient atom.
